Steinbach is not at Pier 46 and has not been since that evening. The room was left tidy and the bed was not slept in. The bells rang the half hour at 8:00 PM. The sexton rings them off the sacristy clock and it keeps good time.
Nobody can put it closer than between 6:30 PM and 8:00 PM, which is two hours of nothing useful. The precinct took a statement and filed it. A grown person is allowed to go where they like.
A pasted-up timetable is gone from the ferry slip. The timetable has been pulled off the wall, and the corner of it is still pasted there.
Weisglass puts Steinbach at the Hallam when the lights went, which was 7:30 PM, and in no hurry to be anywhere.

Grasso says Steinbach told Wehrle that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found at the walk-up: A typed page of dates and sums in Steinbach’s file, headed with Hochstetter’s name.
Pickering says Steinbach told Hochstetter that the story would run whether Hochstetter liked it or not.
Found at the ferry slip: A lease assignment made out in Ruggiero’s name, waiting only on Steinbach’s signature.

Ledger pages at the walk-up where the totals have been rubbed and written over.
The bank confirms the account: Wehrle has been taking two hundred a month for a year, and was at the walk-up doing exactly that from 10:30 PM to 11:00 PM. It is theft, and it is not murder.
The books at the walk-up settle it. Wehrle spent from 10:30 PM to 11:00 PM covering a hole in the accounts, which is why Wehrle would rather be suspected of anything else.
